subtitle: How merchants of many countries turned roads and seas into their only homeland

panels.shot: wide, low-angle view of a busy medieval South Indian port, with Nanadesi Merchant standing at the edge of a wooden jetty, ships and nagaram town behind, distant shoreline across the bay
panels.action: Nanadesi Merchant stands in three-quarter profile on a bustling wharf, one hand on a bales-laden cart and the other shading his eyes toward ships on the Bay of Bengal, with a hilltop temple town rising behind him.

dialogue.text: In an age of kingdoms and castes, the Nanadesi called themselves people of many countries; how did merchants build a road without borders, yet keep its gates so tightly guarded?

i18n.hi: राज और जात के दौर में भी नानदेशी अपने को कई देसों के लोग कहते थे; फिर उन्होंने बिना सरहद की राह कैसे बनाई, पर फाटक इतने कसे कैसे रखे?

panels.shot: bird's-eye view over the Deccan, tracking a long caravan road weaving between rivers, temples and market towns
panels.action: A long line of pack-bullocks and carts winds along a dusty road below, led by Nanadesi Merchant on horseback, passing stone shrines and milestone pillars etched with faint inscriptions.

dialogue.text: From the eleventh to the thirteenth century, roads from the Kaveri to the Krishna shook with caravans; in the stone records of these routes, a new name appears again and again—Nanadesi, people of many countries.

i18n.hi: ग्यारहवीं से तेरहवीं सदी तक कावेरी से कृष्णा तक की राहें काफिलों से काँप उठीं; इन्हीं रास्तों की पत्थर-लिपियों में बार‑बार उभरता है एक नाम—नानदेशी, यानी कई देसों के लोग।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a crowded nagaram street, camera at eye level between stalls
panels.action: Nanadesi Merchant walks through a dense nagaram market street lined with cloth-dealers, grain sellers and metalworkers, while a stone pillar inscription stands at a crossroads beside a temple gateway.

dialogue.text: Their inscriptions call them residents of nagarams—market towns linked to temples and guild-houses; here, in the noise of coin and scale, distance itself became a profession.

i18n.hi: उनकी शिलालेखों में वे ‘नगरम्’ के बाशिंदे कहलाते हैं—मंदिरों और श्रेणी‑मंडपों से जुड़ी बाज़ार बस्तियाँ; यहाँ सिक्कों और तराजू की गूँज में दूरी ही एक पेशा बन गई।

panels.shot: close-up on carved stone inscription, with Nanadesi Merchant's hand tracing the letters
panels.action: Nanadesi Merchant kneels by a weathered stone slab, fingers lightly following ancient Grantha and Tamil letters that mention Nanadesi alongside other guild names like Ainnurruvar.

dialogue.text: Some stones pair Nanadesi with the great federations—the Ainnurruvar, the Five Hundred of the Thousand Settlements; were they a separate guild, or a rank within these mighty networks?

i18n.hi: कुछ पत्थरों पर नानदेशी का नाम जुड़ता है बड़ी संघों से—ऐन्नूर्रुवर, हज़ार बस्तियों की पाँच सौ मंडली; क्या वे अलग श्रेणी थे, या इन्हीं महा‑जालों के अंदर एक ऊँचा ओहदा?

panels.shot: interior wide shot of a guild hall, with beams and lamps, low-angle emphasizing height
panels.action: Nanadesi Merchant sits cross-legged in a timbered guild hall with other richly dressed merchants, palm-leaf documents spread before them, as a lamp-lit shrine niche glows behind.

dialogue.text: Later scholars debate their nature: were these guilds true corporations with rigid boards and seals, or flexible titles of prestige, claimed when a merchant’s reach spanned many lands?

i18n.hi: बाद के विद्वान बहसते हैं—ये संघ सचमुच सख़्त निगम थे, मुहरों और कड़े बोर्डों वाले, या फिर लचीले मान‑खिताब, जो वही पाता जब किसी व्यापारी की पहुँच कई देसों तक फैल जाती?

panels.shot: map-like overhead composition, but rendered as real terrain with caravans and ships, no modern borders
panels.action: The panel blends terrain views: caravans crossing a dry plateau, a river port with boats, and an open sea with lateen-rigged ships, all linked by faint, glowing paths that meet at the small figure of Nanadesi Merchant at the center.

dialogue.text: What the records agree on is movement: Nanadesis appear along routes from Karnataka to Tamil country, across Andhra coasts, in Kerala ports, and even on stones raised in Sri Lanka.

i18n.hi: इतिहास जिन बातों पर एकमत है, वह है चलन; नानदेशी के नाम कर्नाटक से तमिल देस की राहों पर, आंध्र तटों पर, केरल के बंदरगाहों में, और श्रीलंका की शिलाओं पर भी उभरते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot at a temple courtyard, slight low-angle to include gopuram
panels.action: Nanadesi Merchant stands before a towering temple gopuram, handing a cloth-wrapped bundle to a priest while scribes sit nearby, recording a donation on palm leaves beside a granite inscription in progress.

dialogue.text: Inscription after inscription ties them to temple endowments—land grants, lamps, feeding houses; the guild’s road without borders still anchored itself in stone, ritual and local gods.

i18n.hi: एक के बाद एक शिलालेख उन्हें मंदिर दान से जोड़ता है—जागीर, दीप, अन्नछत्र; यह बे‑सरहद राह भी पत्थर, पूजा और देसी देवताओं से ही जकड़ी रही।

panels.shot: wide shot at a coastal nagaram, with both land and sea activities visible
panels.action: Nanadesi Merchant oversees porters loading pepper sacks and textiles onto a wooden ship at a lagoon, while behind him tiled-roof warehouses, a nagaram gate and a line of bullocks stand waiting.

dialogue.text: Their wealth rode both bullock and wave; around the Bay of Bengal, ports saw Nanadesi names in gifts and guild pacts, linking inland markets to overseas buyers and sailors.

i18n.hi: उनकी दौलत बैलगाड़ी पर भी दौड़ी, लहरों पर भी; बंगाल की खाड़ी के इर्द‑गिर्द बंदरगाहों में नानदेशी नाम दान और शर्तनामों पर चमके, जो भीतरी बाज़ारों को समंदर‑पार खरीदारों और मल्लाहों से जोड़ते थे।

panels.shot: dynamic three-quarter shot on ship deck, horizon tilted slightly to suggest swell
panels.action: Nanadesi Merchant stands on the creaking deck of a broad-hulled ship, looking back toward the faint line of the Coromandel coast as sailors haul ropes and a carved masthead points toward Sri Lanka.

dialogue.text: On some stones in Sri Lanka, Nanadesi stand beside Tamil merchant names and local donors; the road without borders had crossed the waters, but it still spoke in familiar scripts and deities.

i18n.hi: श्रीलंका की कुछ शिलाओं पर नानदेशी तमिल सौदागरों और स्थानीय दाताओं के साथ खड़े दिखते हैं; बे‑सरहद राह सागर पार कर गई, पर बोली अब भी वही लिपियाँ और वही देवता थीं।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot in a guild-house courtyard at dusk
panels.action: Nanadesi Merchant sits under a neem tree in a guild courtyard, sharing betel and quiet conversation with another merchant while young apprentices listen, a chest of weights and coins open beside them.

dialogue.speaker: Nanadesi Merchant
dialogue.text: Our home is not a village, brother. It is the route itself.

i18n.hi: अपना गाँव नहीं, भैया—अपना घर तो यही राह है।

panels.shot: close-up on Nanadesi Merchant's face, half-lit by lamp, introspective expression
panels.action: In lamplight, Nanadesi Merchant’s face shows both pride and caution as he counts coins into neat stacks, shadows of caste marks and jewelry falling across his hands.

dialogue.text: Yet this mobile identity did not wash away hierarchy; inscriptions hint at caste limits and closed circles, where guild honor protected its own more than the many who labored for them.

i18n.hi: पर यह चलायमान पहचान सारी ऊँच‑नीच नहीं बहा ले गई; पत्थर इशारा करते हैं जात‑की सीमाओं और बंद गोलों की ओर, जहाँ संघ‑इज़्ज़त अपने लोगों को ज़्यादा ढालती थी, उनसे कम जो उनके लिए खटते थे।

panels.shot: wide shot of a bustling port edge, camera low behind anonymous workers
panels.action: From ground level, barefoot porters strain under heavy loads toward a warehouse where Nanadesi Merchant and other guild leaders negotiate calmly under shade, separated by a clear physical distance.

dialogue.text: Port diversity meant many tongues, many faces; it did not always mean equal standing for sailors, porters, artisans or bonded workers who moved the goods that made guilds famous.

i18n.hi: बंदरों की रंग‑बिरंगी भीड़ ने कई बोली, कई चेहरे दिए; पर इससे हमेशा नाविक, मज़दूर, कारीगर या बंधुआ हाथों को वही दर्जा नहीं मिला, जिनकी पीठ पर चलकर संघ मशहूर हुए।

panels.shot: medium shot in a royal court hall, with king on throne in background, merchants in foreground
panels.action: Nanadesi Merchant bows before a seated king in a pillared hall, presenting a palm-leaf document, while other courtiers watch and a mural behind shows a caravan and a sea voyage.

dialogue.text: Rulers courted their favor; guild records sit beside royal grants, showing Nanadesi woven into Chola and other South Indian polities, not as subjects alone but as negotiators of routes and revenues.

i18n.hi: राजे‑महाराजे उनकी मेहर चाहने लगे; संघ‑लिपियाँ राजदान‑पत्रों के साथ दिखाई देती हैं, दिखाती हैं कि नानदेशी चोल और दूसरे दक्षिणी राज्यों में सिर्फ़ रैयत नहीं, राह और महसूल के सौदागर भी थे।

panels.shot: transition shot, time-lapse feel, same nagaram street at different times, slightly ghosted
panels.action: The same nagaram street appears layered in time—once crowded and bright with Nanadesi merchants, then more faded with different traders and empty guild houses, as Nanadesi Merchant’s figure becomes a faint outline.

dialogue.text: By the later medieval centuries, other powers and routes rose; the Nanadesi name fades from some stones, but the pattern they carved—mobile networks bound by trust and ritual—endured in newer forms.

i18n.hi: देर मध्यकाल तक नई ताकतें और राहें उठीं; कहीं‑कहीं पत्थरों से नानदेशी नाम धुंधला गया, पर जो नक्शा उन्होंने काटा—चलती फिरती जालियाँ, भरोसे और रीत से बंधी—नई शक्लों में जीता रहा।

panels.shot: close-up on an old stone inscription half-buried, with modern feet passing by, soft focus
panels.action: A weathered inscription naming Nanadesi lies half-buried at the edge of a modern-looking path, as only the sandals of passers-by are visible, walking past without noticing; Nanadesi Merchant's figure is faintly reflected in the stone.

dialogue.text: Today their stones lie quiet beside roads and temples, but each carved word reminds us that long before nations, some Indians learned to live by a road without borders, even while its doors stayed selective.

i18n.hi: आज उनके पत्थर सड़कों और मंदिरों के किनारे चुप पड़े हैं, पर हर खुदा हुआ शब्द याद दिलाता है कि क़ौमों से बहुत पहले ही कुछ भारतीयों ने बे‑सरहद राह पर जीना सीख लिया था, भले उसके दरवाज़े चुने हुए लोगों के लिए ही खुले रहे।

subtitle_i18n.en: How merchants of many countries turned roads and seas into their only homeland
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे कई देसों के सौदागर ने राह और समंदर को ही अपना वतन बनाया
